Hyperreflective foci in the ganglion cell layer, as previously described in gyrate atrophy by Sen et al. [18], were observed in three patients (42.8%). A tilted disc in right eye was also presented (fig 1). Clinical diagnosis identified gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina. He had mild muscle weakness, but his intelligence and electroencephalography (EEG) were normal. Aminoacid analysis revealed a high serum ornithine level (629 nmol/mL), with the normal range being 28-110 nmol/mL. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Fundus photographs in patient diagnosed with gyrate atrophy in adulthood; caption directly attributes confluent peripheral chorioretinal atrophy to this figure panel. b: Autofluorescence images in same gyrate atrophy patient; caption attributes hypoautofluorescence corresponding to atrophy to this panel. c: OCT in same gyrate atrophy case; caption describes multiple intraretinal cystic spaces with preservation of outer retinal layers. No vocabulary finding for cystic spaces, so recorded as proposed_findings; panel still shows specific retinal manifestation of the diagnosed disease.

panels.figure_caption: Multimodal retinal imaging findings. (a) Fundus photography reveals confluent chorioretinal atrophy in the peripheral retina as well as around the arcade vessels (superiorly in the right eye). (b) Fundus autofluorescence imaging demonstrates hypoautofluorescence corresponding to the areas of chorioretinal atrophy. (c) Optical coherence tomography reveals multiple intraretinal cystic spaces with preservation of the outer retinal layers, including the ellipsoid zone.
